subject: Renewal: scaled uptake + bridging credit proposal and banded discount structure
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@nimretail.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@nimretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — scaled uptake + bridging credit idea

Hi Emily / Rajiv,

Thanks again for a productive renewal kickoff last week. Based on our usage analysis and your comments about seasonal uptake, I put together a short proposal to keep pricing predictable while you scale:

- Term: 12-month renewal with the option to expand commits at month 6.
- Banded discounts: graduated discount tiers tied to committed monthly tokens (3 bands: base, growth, scale).
- Bridging credit: a time-limited credit applied to overage during the first 180 days to smooth the transition while you ramp.
- Price hold: guaranteed unit pricing for the first 6 months from the renewal effective date while the bridging credit applies.

I'll attach a one-page summary and a starter pricing matrix for you to review. High-level ask: if Nimbus can commit to a 1.8x average monthly commit across the 12-month term (with a known ramp plan), we can offer an accelerated discount band plus a one-time bridging credit to offset immediate overage risk.

Would you be open to a short call next week to walk through the numbers? If you share a preferred ramp cadence (months 1-3 expected throughput), we can make the matrix concrete.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Emily Carter <emily@nimretail.com>

Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@nimretail.com>, Lisa Chang <lisa.chang@nimretail.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — scaled uptake + bridging credit idea

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear proposal. Quick context from our side:
- Current run-rate: ~180M tokens/month (primarily embeddings + chat generation).
- Expected ramp: +30% by month 3, +80-90% by month 6 (holiday uplift + new personalization work).
- Procurement priorities: predictable unit cost for Q4 and minimal surprise overage charges; short approval window for multi-year lock-ins.

What we care about most is a price hold for the initial ramp window and a clear credit that offsets the first 3 months of overage if we miss the committed cadence. We can consider a commit increase (1.8x–2x) if the economics are aligned and the first 6 months have protection.

Can you confirm: 1) rough size of the bridging credit relative to expected overage, and 2) whether the price hold can be limited to 180 days? If so, we can move to procurement review quickly.

Emily
Emily Carter
Head of ML Platform | Nimbus Retail
emily@nimretail.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@nimretail.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@nimretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Oct 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — scaled uptake + bridging credit idea

Emily — thanks for the clarity. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Bridging credit size: for your projected ramp, we model a credit equal to 60% of forecasted overage for months 1–3 (applied as dollar credits on the invoice). This is a targeted protection, not a full guarantee, designed to reduce near-term cost friction while you ramp capacity.

2) Price hold: yes — we can provide a 180-day price hold on the agreed unit rates for tokens that are within the committed bands. Overage beyond the bridging period or outside the banded tiers will follow the post-hold rates in the contract.

I've attached: bridging_credit_summary.pdf (one-pager) and proposed_pricing_matrix.xlsx (banded tiers + illustrative numbers). Ben — can you review the proposed concessions and confirm internal approvability?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Internal review (Redwood): Ben confirms concession approval + updated pricing matrix.
- Procurement review (Nimbus): Emily / Lisa review attachments and return any redlines.
- Execute amendment + DocuSign for the 12-month term with a 180-day price hold and the bridging credit applied to first invoices.

Would you prefer a 30-minute readout to walk the matrices? I can schedule once Ben confirms numbers.

Marissa

Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — scaled uptake + bridging credit idea

Marissa / team — reviewed the numbers and drafted an updated pricing matrix. Key points: 

- Commit tiers (monthly committed tokens): Base (up to 200M), Growth (200–350M), Scale (350M+).
- Discount bands: 8% / 14% / 20% off list at Base/Growth/Scale respectively given a 12-month commit with 1.8x uplift target.
- Bridging credit: equal to 60% of forecasted overage months 1–3 (applies only if overage > 10% above committed band in that window).
- Price hold: 180 days on unit rates within committed bands; after hold, rates step to a predefined schedule tied to band shrink/expansion clauses.

I attached pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx with cell-level commentary: highlighted the approval-necessary concessions (bridging credit cap and the overage threshold). From an approval perspective, we can sign at these levels with Revenue Manager signoff, but anything above 65% bridging credit or a longer hold will need Sales Leadership approval.

Ben

Emily / Rajiv / Lisa — quick update and next steps: 

Thanks for the quick review, everyone. We converged internally on the attached pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx and are ready to move forward under these terms: 

- 12-month renewal effective 2027-11-01 with a 180-day price hold on committed band rates.
- Commit: target 1.8x current average run-rate (nominal monthly commit set in amendment).
- Bridging credit: 60% of forecasted overage months 1–3, applied as invoice credits; capped per the matrix.
- Additional: standard SLA language, the ability to increase commit mid-term with pro-rated pricing, and a mutual exit clause for force majeure events.

Next steps:
